title: The Heartless Theme (a.k.a. The Superglue Riddim)
label: East West
format: CD single (per OCC catalogue); also track 14 on disc 1 of the mix album Heartless Crew Presents Crisp Biscuit Vol 1 (East West, May 2002)
producers: Heartless Crew (Trench calls it the crew's only original production on the mix CD)

type.basis: FACT (2013): too spartan to be called garage, too breezy to qualify as grime. Recorded exactly on the boundary.

sound.text: Trench (2022): high-speed patois and a catchy hook; a mission statement for the crew's inclusive, multi-genre approach.
FACT (2013): spartan and bass-heavy, 'Too spartan to be called garage, too breezy to qualify as grime'.

context.text: Official Singles Chart peak no. 21 (first chart date 25 May 2002, 3 weeks); Dance chart peak no. 3.

North London crew (MC Bushkin, MC Mighty Moe, DJ Fonti), on the pirate station Mission 90.6 FM by 1998; Wikipedia says they are credited with paving the way for grime alongside So Solid and Pay As U Go.
Line Noise (2024) calls their 2001 clash with Pay As U Go 'another pivotal moment in the transition from UKG to grime'.
Trench (2022) says it spread mostly via pirate radio, local shops and raves; by 2002 the crew had a 1Xtra Sunday show.

calls.label: between garage and grime ('Too spartan to be called garage, too breezy to qualify as grime')
garage era, linked to UK bass futurism; grime described as arriving just after 2002
shifts between UK garage and grime depending on context
UK garage crew (genres listed include grime)
